goal: Iske baad aap bata sakenge ke koi bhi point (x, y) screen par kahan nazar aata hai, aur kisi shape ki coordinates se uski width, height aur centre nikal sakenge.
warmup: Cricket stadium ke stand ka seating plan sochein: seat A1 upar-left corner mein hai, aap row mein right ki taraf seats ginte hain, aur rows stand mein NEECHE ki taraf jati hain. Dost ko batane ke liye aap kehte hain 'column 40, row 12'. Computer screen bhi aisi hi hai: har chhote dot ka ek column number (x) aur ek row number (y) hota hai, aur ginti upar-left se shuru hoti hai.
definition: Screen chhote dots ki grid hai jinhein pixels kehte hain. Ek point do numbers (x, y) se bataya jata hai. x left edge se pixels ginta hai, y TOP edge se pixels ginta hai. Origin (0, 0) upar-left corner hai. Classic VGA mode mein screen 640 pixels chauri aur 480 pixels oonchi hoti hai, is liye x 0 se 639 tak aur y 0 se 479 tak chalta hai. Functions getmaxx() aur getmaxy() sab se bara x aur sab se bara y dete hain. graphics.h standard C++ nahi hai. Yeh sirf lab PC par Turbo C++ (DOSBox) ya Code::Blocks/Dev-C++ ke saath WinBGIm library mein chalta hai, is liye page ka in-page compiler in programs ko nahi chala sakta. Is page ka canvas ek simulation hai jo woh draw karta hai jo wohi calls draw karti.
howItWorks: Step 1: school ka maths graph bhool jayein: wahan y UPAR jata hai. Screen par y NEECHE jata hai, is liye bara y matlab screen par NEECHE. Step 2: point (x, y) left se x pixels aur top se y pixels door hota hai. Step 3: 640 x 480 screen ka centre taqriban (320, 240) hai. Step 4: kisi bhi rectangle ke liye jis ke corners (left, top) aur (right, bottom) hon, width = right - left, height = bottom - top, aur centre ((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2) hai. Yeh saada hisaab hai, is liye neeche wala console sample sach mein chalta hai. Do drawing samples putpixel, line aur rectangle use karte hain, aur canvas unhein simulate karta hai.
